name: SigmaWaveForm generators
plain: Generate a sequence from a sine, sawtooth, stepped, square or random wave rather than a monotonic schedule. Companion nodes do Fourier filtering, attenuation and a phase-locked loop on sigmas. Because the output isn't descending, the result only makes sense as an experiment or a modulation source.
math: t=linspace(0,1,steps). σ=wave(t; amplitude, frequency) with optional damping and Fourier steps; 'unidirectional' subtracts min (plus min_sigma in the Advanced class).

props.params: steps, amplitude, frequency, damping_factor, waveform_type, enable_unidirectional, min_sigma

label: from code
surprise: 'Unidirectional' only shifts the wave up so it is non-negative; it does not make the sequence descend (sigma_waveform_node.py:69-70).

audit.note: +min_sigma is not Advanced-only: SigmaWaveFormNode also has it (BenNarum__SigmaWaveFormNode/sigma_waveform_node.py:193-194, 342-343); only the Simple class subtracts min alone (line 69). The cited line 72 is the Simple class, which has no Fourier step.
